learn.title: Like sorting a hand of cards
learn.body: Insertion sort keeps the left part sorted. Take the next item and slide it left past every bigger item until it fits. The sorted part then grows by one. A single item is already sorted, so we start at index 1.

learn.title: Insertion sort on {5, 2, 4, 6, 1, 3}
learn.body: Each step inserts the next item into the sorted part.
steps: Insert 6: already bigger than 5, stays. Insert 1: slides to the front. Array: 1 2 4 5 6 3

learn.title: Insertion sort in C
learn.body: `key` is the item being inserted. Bigger items shift one place right to make a gap.

learn.title: Best and worst case
learn.body: If the array is already sorted, each `while` test fails at once, so there are only n - 1 comparisons: $O(n)$. If it is in reverse order, every item slides all the way, giving $n(n-1)/2$ comparisons: $O(n^2)$. For 5 items that is 4 versus 10.
Insertion sort is fast on arrays that are nearly sorted, which is why it is often used for small or almost ordered data.

questions.prompt: Which part of the array does insertion sort keep sorted?
questions.explanation: The sorted part sits on the left and grows by one each round.

questions.prompt: Why does the outer loop start at `i = 1`?
questions.explanation: A single item on its own is trivially in order.

questions.prompt: `{5, 2, 4, 6, 1, 3}`. After inserting the item 2, what is the first item?
questions.explanation: 2 slides past 5, so the array becomes 2 5 4 6 1 3.

questions.prompt: Insertion sort shifts bigger items one place \_\_ to make a gap.
questions.explanation: Items move right so that the key can drop into the gap on the left.

questions.prompt: An already sorted array of 5 items. How many comparisons does insertion sort make?
questions.explanation: One test per item after the first, and each fails at once: 4 comparisons.

questions.prompt: A reverse sorted array of 5 items. How many comparisons?
questions.explanation: Item 2 makes 1, item 3 makes 2, item 4 makes 3 and item 5 makes 4: 10.

questions.prompt: Which input is best for insertion sort?
choices: An array of all different primes
questions.explanation: Sorted input needs almost no shifting, so the cost is $O(n)$.
